findings.text: The eval at line 46 executes arbitrary code from the --description argument. A test description like '$(malicious_cmd)' or '`cmd`' would be executed during parsing.
The removed bats_test_begin() function previously called setup() for each test. Without it, test setup code never runs, breaking all tests that rely on setup().
BATS_TEST_DESCRIPTION is only set when the test name matches (line 68 condition). Tests that don't match will have an empty or stale BATS_TEST_DESCRIPTION, breaking test reporting.
Calling bats_test_function without --description or --tags (e.g., just a test name) hits the *) case and exits with error. This breaks existing calls that pass only a test name.

0.reason: The eval at line 46 executes the --description argument as shell code, allowing command substitution or arbitrary commands in the description to run during parsing.

1.reason: The setup() call was moved to a different location in the change (likely in bats-exec-test), so the removal of bats_test_begin() does not necessarily break setup() execution.

2.reason: This finding describes the same root cause as the reference bug: the condition at line 68 uses unquoted $* which fails to match test names with spaces, leaving BATS_TEST_DESCRIPTION unset for such tests.

3.reason: The new code requires --description or --tags options, but the reference bug is about the matching condition, not the option parsing; this is a deliberate interface change, not a defect.
